families.name: Dense
families.summary: Every parameter is used for every token.
families.how: Each layer has one attention block and one feed-forward block. A token passes through all of them.
families.why: It is the simplest design to serve and has the widest runtime support.
families.watch: Compute cost rises directly with model size, because nothing is skipped.

families.name: Sparse MoE
families.summary: A very large model where only a small share of the parameters runs for each token.
families.how: The feed-forward block is split into many experts. A small router picks a few experts for each token.
families.why: It adds capacity without a matching rise in compute per token.
families.watch: Plan memory for total parameters and compute for active parameters. All experts must stay loaded even though few run.

families.name: Sparse hybrid
families.summary: Mixes cheaper non-standard layers with some full attention, and runs only part of the model per token.
families.how: Most layers use linear attention or convolution. A smaller number of attention layers keep exact long-range lookups.
families.why: It lowers the memory and compute cost of very long contexts.
families.watch: These layer types need specific runtime support. Confirm that your serving stack implements them before committing.

families.name: Dense hybrid
families.summary: Mixes different layer types, with every parameter active for every token.
families.how: Attention layers alternate with linear attention, convolution or state-space layers. There is no expert routing.
families.why: It reduces context cost while keeping compute predictable, which suits smaller models.
families.watch: Runtime support varies by layer type, so test on your target hardware.

families.name: Hybrid MoE
families.summary: State-space layers carry most of the sequence, with a few attention layers and routed experts.
families.how: Mamba layers interleave with mixture-of-experts layers. A small number of attention layers handle exact lookups.
families.why: State-space layers keep a fixed-size memory, so long contexts cost far less cache.
families.watch: Sessions hold recurrent state, so confirm that state is reset and isolated between users.

families.name: Sparse omnimodal MoE
families.summary: A sparse expert-routed model in the MiMo line, built to work with more than text.
families.how: It uses a sparse MoE backbone with sliding-window and global attention. The MiMo-V2.5 design adds native image, video and audio encoders.
families.why: One model can serve several input types rather than one model per type.
families.watch: Check that the exact checkpoint exposes the input types you need, because official task labels can differ.

families.name: Sparse MoE (causal encoder-decoder)
families.summary: A sparse model whose layers are split into an encoder half and a decoder half.
families.how: The encoder processes the sequence. The decoder's global attention reads its keys and values from the final encoder states.
families.why: Reusing one set of encoder states reduces the attention cache held across decoder layers.
families.watch: This is a rare design, so confirm support in your serving runtime.

families.name: Recurrent
families.summary: No self-attention. Each layer carries a memory state forward from token to token.
families.how: Each token updates a fixed-size matrix memory rather than looking back over earlier tokens.
families.why: Memory does not grow with context length, which suits long streams.
families.watch: Exact recall of earlier text depends on what the state retained, so test long-context tasks directly.

mechanisms.name: Linear attention
mechanisms.summary: Keeps a compact running summary rather than storing every earlier token.
mechanisms.how: Each token updates a fixed-size state. Gated DeltaNet, Kimi Delta Attention and Lightning Attention are variants.
mechanisms.helps: Cache stays flat as context grows.
mechanisms.watch: Recall is approximate, which is why these models keep some full attention layers.
mechanisms.footprint: Greatly reduces attention cache at long context.

source.title: Kimi Linear: An Expressive, Efficient Attention Architecture

mechanisms.name: State-space layers (Mamba)
mechanisms.summary: Processes a sequence through a fixed-size state rather than pairwise token lookups.
mechanisms.how: Each token updates the state, and the output is read from that state.
mechanisms.helps: Long contexts cost little extra memory.
mechanisms.watch: Per-session state must be isolated and reset correctly.
mechanisms.footprint: Fixed state per session instead of a growing cache.

mechanisms.name: Recurrent memory (xLSTM)
mechanisms.summary: An LSTM-style layer with a matrix memory in place of attention.
mechanisms.how: Gates decide what to write to and read from memory at each token.
mechanisms.helps: Memory stays constant regardless of sequence length.
mechanisms.watch: Far fewer production runtimes support it.
mechanisms.footprint: No attention cache, only recurrent state.

mechanisms.name: Convolution blocks
mechanisms.summary: Mixes each token with its immediate neighbours using a short filter.
mechanisms.how: A small kernel slides over the sequence. LIV and ShortConv blocks are the variants used here.
mechanisms.helps: Very cheap, and useful for small models.
mechanisms.watch: Sees only nearby tokens, so it relies on attention layers for long-range context.

mechanisms.name: Multi-token prediction
mechanisms.summary: An extra output path that predicts tokens beyond the next one.
mechanisms.how: Additional prediction modules look further ahead from the same hidden state.
mechanisms.helps: Can improve training and speed up inference through speculative decoding.
mechanisms.watch: Speed gains depend on runtime support for this path.
mechanisms.footprint: Adds a small amount of weight memory.

mechanisms.name: Mixture of experts
mechanisms.summary: Replaces one large feed-forward block with many experts, of which only a few run per token.
mechanisms.how: A router scores the experts for each token and activates the top few.
mechanisms.helps: Adds capacity while keeping compute per token low.
mechanisms.watch: All experts must remain in memory, and traffic across GPUs can become the bottleneck.
mechanisms.footprint: Memory follows total parameters. Compute follows active parameters.

mechanisms.name: Sliding-window and global attention
mechanisms.summary: Most layers look only at recent tokens, and periodic global layers see everything.
mechanisms.how: Local layers keep a fixed window. Every few layers, a global layer attends to the whole context.
mechanisms.helps: Cuts cache and compute at long context.
mechanisms.watch: Facts outside the window reach local layers only through global layers.
mechanisms.footprint: Local layers cache only their window.

mechanisms.name: Sparse attention
mechanisms.summary: Attends only to a selected subset of earlier tokens.
mechanisms.how: A lightweight scorer picks the most relevant tokens, and full attention runs only on those.
mechanisms.watch: Results depend on the selector finding the right tokens.
mechanisms.footprint: Reduces attention compute. Cache savings depend on the design.

mechanisms.name: Gated attention
mechanisms.summary: Each attention head has a learned gate that scales its output.
mechanisms.how: A gate between 0 and 1 controls how much of the attention result is passed on.
mechanisms.helps: Lets the model suppress unhelpful attention and reduces attention sinks.
mechanisms.watch: Adds a small amount of compute to each attention layer.

source.title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models

mechanisms.name: Multi-head latent attention
mechanisms.summary: Compresses keys and values into one small shared representation.
mechanisms.how: The cache stores a compact latent vector, which is expanded when attention runs.
mechanisms.helps: Greatly reduces the attention cache per token.
mechanisms.watch: Needs dedicated kernels to run efficiently, so check runtime support.

mechanisms.name: Grouped-query attention
mechanisms.summary: Many query heads share a smaller number of key and value heads.
mechanisms.how: Query heads are divided into groups, and each group reads from one shared key-value head.
mechanisms.helps: Cuts the cache with little quality loss. It is the most common attention type in this catalog.
mechanisms.watch: The cache still grows with every token in context.
mechanisms.footprint: Cache shrinks in proportion to the query-to-KV head ratio.

source.title: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models

mechanisms.name: Multi-head attention
mechanisms.summary: The original transformer attention, where every head stores its own keys and values.
mechanisms.how: Each head compares the current token with all earlier tokens.
mechanisms.watch: Has the largest cache per token of the attention types here.

mechanisms.name: Query-key normalization
mechanisms.summary: Normalizes queries and keys before they are compared.
mechanisms.how: Vectors are scaled to a consistent length, so attention scores stay in a stable range.
mechanisms.watch: It is a detail of the attention block and rarely affects a selection decision.

source.title: Scaling Vision Transformers to 22 Billion Parameters

mechanisms.name: Position encoding
mechanisms.summary: Tells the model where each token sits. RoPE, NoPE and learned bias are the variants here.
mechanisms.how: RoPE rotates queries and keys by an angle based on position, so the angle between two tokens reflects their distance.
mechanisms.helps: RoPE needs no stored position table and handles varying lengths.
mechanisms.watch: NoPE layers rely on causal masking alone for order information.

familyAxes.question: Two design choices place every family: how many of its parameters work on each token, and how each token draws on the tokens before it.

params.name: Dense
params.text: Every parameter works on every token.

params.name: Sparse (mixture of experts)
params.text: A router sends each token to a few experts; most parameters sit idle for any one token.

mixing.name: Attention in every layer
mixing.text: Each layer can look back at earlier tokens directly.

mixing.name: Hybrid
mixing.text: Some layers replace attention with a fixed-size state (linear attention, state-space or convolution).

mixing.name: No attention
mixing.text: Every layer carries a fixed-size memory forward instead.
